[FACT] User is interested in the process of stellar classification.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Observations from telescopes and other instruments are instrumental in the process of stellar classification.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Astronomers use characteristics such as spectral lines and brightness to classify stars into categories that reflect their physical properties.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Spectral lines observed in the spectrum of a star can help determine its temperature, chemical composition, and other properties.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The brightness of a star provides information on its size and distance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Observations are combined to determine a star's classification, such as main sequence star, red giant, or white dwarf.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Observations from telescopes provide vital information necessary for the accurate classification and understanding of stars.  
[USER] What if a star cannot be observed with telescopes? Can it still be classified?  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If a star cannot be observed with telescopes, it is not possible to directly classify it.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Indirect techniques such as gravitational lensing, astrometry, and proper motion measurements can be used to infer properties of unobservable stars.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The gravitational attraction of an invisible companion star can be inferred from its effect on the motion of a visible star.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The luminosity of a distant star can be estimated based on its apparent brightness and assumed distance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Theoretical models can predict physical properties of stars based on mass, size, age, and composition, aiding in classification.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] While direct classification is not possible for unobservable stars, scientific progress can still be made by inferring information.  
[USER] Can you give an example of how theoretical models are used to classify stars?  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Hertzsprung-Russell (HR) diagram is a common theoretical model used to classify stars based on luminosity and surface temperature or spectral type.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The HR diagram helps scientists see the broad properties of stars and their relationships.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Theoretical models create HR diagrams by simulating internal structures of stars and predicting their evolution over time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Factors like mass, composition, and age are taken into account in these models to predict star behavior.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The size of a star is determined by its mass and gas in its core, which helps differentiate between classes of stars.
